## Operator note on scoping and duration (2026-08-23)

The figures above are scoped to this run and report **active** time, not span.
Earlier generations of this report did neither, and showed **173.8h wall clock
and 23.9M billable tokens** — the span of every session that had ever run in
this project directory, including unrelated work from 2026-08-14 and
2026-08-17. `/clear` starts a new conversation but not a new project directory,
so nothing separated them.

Three defects in the skill's tooling, all now fixed:

1. **No lower bound on the transcript read.** `run_meta.run_start()` now derives
   one, preferring a `started` marker that `bootstrap_tmp.sh` writes at the top
   of Phase 1. This run predates that marker, so its value was backfilled from
   the slug directory's birth time (`stat -c %w` → `2026-08-21T16:03:16.678Z`),
   which is what bootstrap would have recorded.
2. **`SUBAGENT_RE` matched only the older `<subagent_tokens>N</subagent_tokens>`
   rendering.** This session's transcript uses `subagent_tokens: N` inside a
   `<usage>` block, so every subagent result went uncounted. The 7,596,926
   subagent tokens the unscoped report once showed were entirely from the
   2026-08-17 sessions and never belonged to this research.
3. **Duration was reported as wall clock only.** Span measures how long a
   session sat open, which for unattended work is unbounded and says nothing
   about effort. `active` sums only the gaps below 30 minutes.

**Why 30 minutes.** Measured against this run's own transcript: the longest gap
that was genuinely work was 14.7 minutes — a slow subagent — and the next gap up
was 48.5 hours, the break between the two sittings. Every threshold from 15 to
60 minutes returns the same answer, so the figure is not an artefact of the
knob. The report prints the excluded-gap count and the largest excluded gap so
that stays checkable on runs with different shapes.

**Read the two numbers as:** this research took about **2.1 hours of work**,
spread across two sittings two days apart. Neither defect affected any finding
in the deliverable.
